claim: Full batch GD computes all per-example gradients at the same parameters and takes their average
notes: Average empirical loss; n samples; not one example at a time

claim: Single-example SGD uses a randomly sampled example gradient in each iteration
notes: Practical random reshuffling differs in independence from with-replacement assumption

claim: SGD diminishing gains may be subject to sums of learning rates divergent and squared gains summable
notes: Convergence requires additional objective/noise assumptions; schedule alone insufficient

claim: Robbins and Monro developed a general stochastic approximation root-finding method in 1951
notes: Do not claim the 1951 paper introduced minibatch GPU neural network training

claim: In the fixed quadratic example with a=[-3,1,3,7] at theta=0, the gradients are [3,-1,-3,-7] and their mean is -2
notes: Not original paper data; elementary derivative theta-a_i

claim: Uniform with-replacement selection produces an unbiased gradient estimate of finite-sum empirical risk at fixed theta
locator: SG general theory; independent finite-sum derivation in post
notes: Unbiased conditional on fixed theta and uniform sampling; not all practical data samplers

claim: For independent identically distributed per-example gradient noise, minibatch mean covariance decreases as Sigma/B
locator: Minibatch SGD discussion and elementary covariance identity
notes: Not a universal rule with correlated, stratified or without-replacement samples

claim: Bottou discusses approximation, estimation and optimization errors under finite computational budgets
notes: Theory tradeoff is not proof SGD universally wins in predictive accuracy

claim: Bottou's RCV1 hinge loss linear SVM comparison has SGD 1.4 seconds / 6.02 percent test error and SVMPERF 66 seconds / 6.03 percent test error
notes: Original experiment, incomparable with modern GPU throughput

claim: The ALPHA squared hinge loss task uses 100000 samples with 500 normalized input variables
notes: The original benchmark is a linear SVM, not transformer training

claim: The CONLL chunking CRF experiment reports test loss and test F1 comparing SGD, SGDQN and ASGD
notes: ASGD does not attain asymptotic promise in this task

claim: Bottou discusses Polyak Juditsky averaged stochastic gradients separately from vanilla SGD
notes: ASGD averages iterates; not identical to momentum

claim: The PyTorch SGD optimizer supports momentum, dampening, Nesterov and weight decay options
notes: Modern implementation options rather than Bottou 2010 bare SGD update

claim: Hand-drawn noisy path and learning-rate curves are pedagogical figures, not recorded experimental trajectories
